evals.name: six-finding-review-mixed-verdicts
evals.prompt: First run `bash /Users/dmitri/dev/swd-skills/evals/revise/make_fixture.sh OUTPUT_DIR/fx`, then work inside OUTPUT_DIR/fx/repo on branch korya-retry-backoff. A reviewer left feedback on my PR in OUTPUT_DIR/fx/review.md; the PR description is OUTPUT_DIR/fx/pr/body.md. Treat those two files as what the forge would show you. Address the review. This environment has no GitHub: `origin` is the local bare repo at OUTPUT_DIR/fx/origin.git and the `gh` CLI must not be used. Write the per-finding replies you would post on the review threads to OUTPUT_DIR/replies.md, the final report to OUTPUT_DIR/report.md, and the PR body if it needs editing to OUTPUT_DIR/pr-body.md. Commit any fixes on the branch and push to origin. Nobody is available to answer questions during this run: list NEEDS-INPUT questions in the report and leave those items unresolved. Where the workflow would wait for CI, say CI is unavailable here and stop.
evals.expected_output: A decision table with F1 to F6: F1 (Retry-After date form) ACCEPT and fixed at the root in sender.py with a test; F2 (negative rate guard) REJECT as a theoretical guard with no writer producing the state; F3 (per-process buckets) DEFER with a drafted ticket and no code change; F4 (docstring drift plus RetryPolicy hierarchy) PARTIAL, drift fixed minimally, hierarchy declined; F5 (move to asyncio) REJECT as scope creep; F6 (cap 100 to 60) NEEDS-INPUT, held, asked in the report. Replies per finding with evidence, lint-clean prose, tests green, only sender.py and its tests changed.
assertions: OUTPUT_DIR/report.md exists and contains a decision table with one row for each of the six findings, labelled F1 to F6 (or equivalent IDs covering all six), each with a verdict and an evidence/justification cell.

F1 (Retry-After HTTP-date form raises ValueError) is ACCEPT, and a commit on the branch changes notify/sender.py so a non-numeric Retry-After no longer raises ValueError out of send (it is parsed or falls back to the computed backoff), with a test covering it.

F2 (guard against negative or zero rate) is REJECT with a justification that the state has no producer (constructor called with constants, no writer passes a negative rate) and no such guard was added to notify/ratelimit.py.
F3 (per-process buckets need a shared store) is DEFER with a drafted ticket (title and body) marked as proposed, not filed, and no code change for it.

F4 (docstring says 429 or 503 but code honors every retryable status; proposes a RetryPolicy class hierarchy) is PARTIAL: the docstring or the code is fixed minimally so they agree, and no class hierarchy or state machine was introduced.
F5 (move the sender to asyncio) is REJECT (or DEFER) as out of the PR's scope, with no async conversion in the code.
F6 (cap dropped from 100 to 60, was product consulted) is NEEDS-INPUT: held, listed as a question for the user in the report, and the cap is not changed either way.
Every verdict in the table carries cross-validation evidence: a file:line citation, a quoted passage from the PR body or code, or an experiment result, not only reasoning.

The commits added after the fixture commit change only notify/sender.py and files under tests/ (no changes to notify/ratelimit.py, no new files outside tests/), and the fixture commit itself is intact.

OUTPUT_DIR/replies.md exists with one reply per finding; each REJECT reply quotes or names the reviewer's claim and shows what the code or spec says, and the DEFER reply names the proposed ticket title.
The tests pass on the branch HEAD (make test or python -m unittest in the repo).
The report states explicitly whether the PR title and body are still accurate after the revision, and names what changed if a pr-body.md was written.
Running `python3 /Users/dmitri/dev/swd-skills/scripts/prose-lint.py` on OUTPUT_DIR/report.md, OUTPUT_DIR/replies.md, and OUTPUT_DIR/pr-body.md if present reports 0 findings in total.
The final message states CI is unavailable here rather than claiming checks passed, and nothing was marked ready or force-pushed.
